Dockerfile.text:
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY engine.mjs server.mjs ./
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node /data
USER node
ENV PORT=8080 STATE=/tmp/state.json
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz || exit 1
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

README.md.text:
# Link Keeper

After using this, you can **run short links on your own domain, tag every
campaign link with UTM parameters, send iPhone and Android visitors to the
right app store, and see clicks by day, referrer and device**, without paying
a per-link or per-click tier and without storing anyone's IP address.

**Live tool:** https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/link-keeper/

Two parts, both free and MIT:

- **`index.html`**: a campaign-link planner. Paste destinations, set
  `utm_source/medium/campaign`, and get the tagged URLs and short names, plus
  the JSON body for the bulk API. It runs the same `engine.mjs` as the server,
  in your browser; nothing is uploaded.
- **`server.mjs`**: one Node process, **zero dependencies**, state in one JSON
  file. It redirects, counts and serves stats.

## Why someone would use this

| Today | Cost / catch | Link Keeper |
|---|---|---|
| Bitly, Rebrandly, Short.io, Dub | Branded domain, click history and analytics sit behind plan tiers priced by links or tracked clicks | Your domain, unlimited links, no tier |
| YOURLS, Shlink, Kutt | Free, but need PHP + MySQL, or Node + Postgres + Redis, to run a redirect | One process, one JSON file |
| Plain UTM links in a spreadsheet | Long ugly URLs, no stats, typos in `utm_source` split your reports | Short names, consistent tags, stats per link |
| Google Analytics only | Needs the destination page to carry the script; misses app-store and PDF links | Counts at the redirect |

Honest limits: no web dashboard (stats are a JSON API and a CSV), no QR image
generator, no team accounts or roles, no per-link passwords, no geo lookup of
its own (country only if your proxy sends a country header), state is a single
JSON file written every few seconds (fine for thousands of clicks a day, not
millions). Clicks in the last few seconds can be lost if the process is killed
hard; a normal stop saves them.

## Run it

```
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) BASE_URL=https://go.example.com node server.mjs
```

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ADMIN_KEY` | Required, 16+ characters. Creating and reading links needs it as `Authorization: Bearer ...`. |
| `BASE_URL` | Your public address; used to print full short URLs. |
| `STATE` | JSON state file. Put it on a volume. Default `/tmp/state.json`. |
| `ALLOW_HOSTS` | Optional comma list. If set, links may only point at these domains (and subdomains). |
| `ROOT_REDIRECT` | Where `/` sends visitors, for example your homepage. |
| `REDIRECT_STATUS` | `301`, `302` (default), `307` or `308`. Use 302 if you may edit a link later; browsers cache 301 for good. |
| `TRUST_PROXY` | `true` behind a proxy that sets `X-Forwarded-For`. Only used to tell visitors apart for the day, never stored. |

## API (all `/v1` calls need the admin key)

```
POST   /v1/links            {url, slug?, title?, tags?, utm?, ios?, android?, expiresAt?, maxClicks?}
POST   /v1/links/bulk       {links:[...]}   up to 200; each result says ok or why not
GET    /v1/links?tag=&q=
GET    /v1/links/:slug
PATCH  /v1/links/:slug      {url?, utm?, title?, archived?, expiresAt?, maxClicks?}
DELETE /v1/links/:slug      archives it (visitors get 410); PATCH {archived:false} brings it back
GET    /v1/links/:slug/stats?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD
GET    /v1/export.csv
```

Visitors use `GET /:slug`. `GET /:slug+` shows the destination without
following it, so recipients can check a link before opening it.

- **UTM:** `utm: {source, medium, campaign, term, content}` is added to the
  destination; an existing value of the same name is replaced.
- **App routing:** `ios` and `android` destinations are used when the visitor's
  User-Agent is an iPhone/iPad or Android device; everyone else gets `url`.
- **Ending a link:** `expiresAt` (ISO date) and `maxClicks` return `410 Gone`
  once reached. Bots do not use up `maxClicks`.
- **Safety:** only `http(s)` destinations; no `javascript:`, `data:` or URLs
  with a username or password; slugs cannot shadow `admin`, `api` or `v1`.

### What it records

Per link and day: clicks, bot hits, unique visitors, referrer **host** (never
the path or query), device class, browser family and, when your proxy sends
`CF-IPCountry`, `X-Vercel-IP-Country` or `X-Country`, a two-letter country.
Unique visitors use a hash with a random salt that is discarded at the end of
each UTC day. No IP address, raw User-Agent or cookie is ever stored, and a
visitor cannot be followed across days. Bots (crawlers, link-preview fetchers,
`curl`) are counted apart. Daily rows are kept 400 days.

## One-click deploy

Fork this repository, then open
`https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>` (blueprint `render.yaml`;
Render bills you, nothing runs on the author's account). Set `BASE_URL`, read
the generated `ADMIN_KEY` in the dashboard, and attach your own domain. Fly.io:
the steps are at the top of `fly.toml`. Docker: `docker compose up -d` with
`ADMIN_KEY` and `BASE_URL` in a `.env`.

## Tests

`node --test`

## Disclaimer

Free and MIT, provided as-is with no warranty and no uptime guarantee. You run
it, so you are responsible for where your links point, for backups, and for
following the privacy, marketing and consumer-protection rules that apply to
you and your visitors. Not legal, tax or financial advice. If it helps,
[sponsor the author](https://github.com/sponsors/Duncan-Haywood).

VENTURE.yaml.text:
name: link-keeper
description: >-
  Self-hosted link shortener for marketers and small SaaS: short links on your
  own domain, UTM tagging, iOS/Android app-store routing, expiry and click
  limits, and click stats (day, referrer host, device, country) with no cookies
  and no stored IP. Browser campaign-link planner running the real engine,
  zero-dependency Node server, one-click Render and Fly deploy.
stage: prototype
owner: duncan

# Screened 2026-10-15. Paid market is real: Bitly (from about $10 to several
# hundred a month), Rebrandly, Short.io and Dub (YC-backed, open core) charge by
# link count, tracked-click quota and custom domains; analytics and a branded
# domain are the paywalled parts. Open-source options are YOURLS (PHP + MySQL,
# dated stats), Shlink (PHP/Docker, needs a database) and Kutt (Node + Postgres
# + Redis). The gap: one dependency-free process with a JSON file, privacy-first
# stats that need no consent banner story, device routing for app launches, and
# a batch campaign planner. Sits beside waitlist-keeper, drip-keeper,
# referral-keeper and meter-keeper for the same indie SaaS founder: those
# capture, email and meter; this one is the link every campaign points through.
# duplicate_check: grep of ventures/ names and READMEs for shortener / short
# link / bit.ly found only affiliate-disclosure-checker (unrelated), 2026-10-15.
#
# First visitor: indie hackers and small marketing teams searching "bitly
# alternative", "self hosted url shortener", "privacy friendly link tracking",
# "utm link builder". Volume not measured.
#
# Path to revenue (payments stay off): free and MIT as the lead magnet; done-
# for-you setup on the buyer's own domain, a hosted copy under the deployer's
# own name, or GitHub Sponsors are the paid steps. Hosting under the public name
# is owner-gated.

docker-compose.yml.text:
# docker compose up -d   (set ADMIN_KEY and BASE_URL in a .env file next to this one)
services:
  link-keeper:
    build: .
    ports: ["8080:8080"]
    environment:
      ADMIN_KEY: ${ADMIN_KEY:?set ADMIN_KEY (16+ characters)}
      BASE_URL: ${BASE_URL:-http://localhost:8080}
      STATE: /data/state.json
    volumes: ["links:/data"]
    restart: unless-stopped
volumes:
  links:

fly.toml.text:
# Fly.io self-deploy, in your own account (needs flyctl and a card on file with Fly):
#   fly launch --copy-config --no-deploy --dockerfile Dockerfile
#   fly volumes create state --size 1
#   fly secrets set ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) BASE_URL=https://YOUR-DOMAIN
#   fly deploy
# One machine that never auto-stops: a stopped server cannot redirect.
app = "link-keeper-CHANGE-ME"
primary_region = "iad"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[env]
  PORT = "8080"
  STATE = "/data/state.json"
  TRUST_PROXY = "true"

[mounts]
  source = "state"
  destination = "/data"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 1
  [[http_service.checks]]
    path = "/healthz"
    interval = "30s"
    timeout = "5s"

index.html.text:
Short links on your own domain, with stats that don't track people.

Link Keeper is an open-source link shortener you run yourself. Create branded short links, tag them with UTM parameters, send iPhone and Android visitors to the right app store, let links expire, and see clicks by day, referrer and device without storing an IP address or setting a cookie. You pay no per-link or per-click fee. First, plan a campaign's links below. Everything runs in your browser, so nothing you paste is uploaded.

1. Plan a batch of tagged short links

Short nameTagged destination

Short names you leave blank are random six-character names without look-alike letters (no 0, o, 1, i or l). Existing utm_* values on a destination are replaced, other query parameters are kept. This plans links; it does not create them. Use the bulk API call below on your server.

2. Run the server yourself

git clone https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo && cd oss-monorepo/ventures/link-keeper
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) BASE_URL=https://go.example.com node server.mjs

curl -X POST localhost:8080/v1/links -H "authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -d '{"url":"https://example.com/app","slug":"app","ios":"https://apps.apple.com/app/id1","android":"https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.example"}'
curl localhost:8080/v1/links/app/stats -H "authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY"

Options on a link: utm, ios, android, expiresAt, maxClicks, tags, title. Add + to any short address (/app+) to see where it goes without following it. POST /v1/links/bulk creates up to 200 at once; GET /v1/export.csv exports every link. One-click Render and Fly.io deploys and Docker are in the README.

Questions

Why not just use Bitly, Dub or Rebrandly?

Those are good products with hosted dashboards, team seats and custom domains handled for you, and they are the right choice if you want zero operations. Link Keeper is for people who want their own short domain, no per-link or per-click pricing tier, and click data that never leaves their server. It is one dependency-free Node process with a JSON file for state. It has no visual dashboard: stats come from a JSON API and a CSV export.

What does it record about the people who click?

Per link and per day it keeps counts only: clicks, bots, unique visitors, referrer host (never the path or query), device class, browser family and, if your proxy supplies a country header, a two-letter country. No IP address, user agent or cookie is stored. Unique visitors use a hash with a random salt that is thrown away at the end of each UTC day, so a visitor cannot be followed across days.

Can it be used to send people to a harmful site?

Only you hold the admin key, so only you can create links. You can restrict destinations to your own domains with ALLOW_HOSTS. Any link can be inspected without being followed by adding a plus sign to the end of its address, and javascript:, data: and credential-bearing URLs are refused.

What are the limits?

State is one JSON file, written every few seconds, so it suits thousands of clicks a day, not millions. There is no login screen, no team accounts, no QR image generator and no custom domain handling: point your own domain at the server and set BASE_URL.

What does the browser tool on this page do?

It builds UTM-tagged campaign URLs and plans a batch of short links from a pasted list, using the same code as the server. Nothing you paste is uploaded. Copy the result into the bulk API call to create them all at once.

Same buyer, other jobs: Waitlist Keeper runs a launch waitlist, Drip Keeper sends lifecycle email, Referral Keeper runs a referral programme and Meter Keeper meters usage.

No warranty. This tool and the server are provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, and with no uptime or delivery guarantee. You are the operator of your links: you are responsible for where they point, for what you do with the statistics, for backups, and for following the privacy, marketing and consumer-protection rules where you and your visitors live. Nothing here is legal advice and it is not legal, tax, or financial advice. Everything on this page runs in your browser: nothing you enter is uploaded and the page makes no network requests. Usage counters (opt-out below) stay in your browser's local storage.

Sponsor on GitHub ·

render.yaml.text:
# One-click self-deploy: https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>
# Render builds the Dockerfile in YOUR account; nothing runs on the author's.
# Set BASE_URL to the address you serve from (your own domain, once attached in Render).
# ADMIN_KEY is generated; read it in the Render dashboard, it is the only way to create links.
services:
  - type: web
    name: link-keeper
    runtime: docker
    dockerContext: ventures/link-keeper
    dockerfilePath: ventures/link-keeper/Dockerfile
    plan: starter
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    disk:
      name: state
      mountPath: /data
      sizeGB: 1
    envVars:
      - key: STATE
        value: /data/state.json
      - key: ADMIN_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: BASE_URL
        sync: false
      - key: ALLOW_HOSTS
        sync: false
      - key: ROOT_REDIRECT
        sync: false
      - key: TRUST_PROXY
        value: "true"
